statement.p: If C is the line segment from (2,1) to, (0,0), find the value of the line integral:

p.m: \int_C (7 y^2\,\vec i + 3 x\,\vec j)\cdot d\vec r =

static.solution:
(0,0) to (2,1) and then take the negative. The line segment is parameterized by x = 2 t\quad y = t, \qquad \mbox{for } 0\le t\le 1.
Then \vec r'(t)=2\vec i+ \vec j, so \int_C (7 y^2\,\vec i + 3 x\,\vec j)\cdot d\vec r =-\int_0^1\left(7 t^2\,\vec i + 6 t\,\vec j \right)\cdot (2\vec i+\vec j)\, dt =-\int_0^1(14 t^2 + 6 t)\, dt=-\left(\frac{14}{3} t^3 + 3 t^2\right)\bigg|_0^1 = -\frac{23}{3}.
